# Glossary: property, BBMP and GST terms used in Bengaluru

> Plain-language definitions of the terms Bengaluru property owners and businesses meet: Khata, A Khata, B Khata, e-Khata, e-Aasthi, EPID, Encumbrance Certificate, RTC/Pahani, mutation, bifurcation, DC conversion, guidance value, occupancy certificate, GSTIN, GSTR-2B, ITC, ASMT-10, DRC-01A, sections 73 and 74, APL-01.

Source: https://www.marvelconsultants.co.in/glossary/  ·  Organisation: Marvel Consultants, Bengaluru  ·  Phone: +91 91875 98642  ·  WhatsApp: https://wa.me/919187598642  ·  Last reviewed: 2026-08-29

Short definitions, written for owners and finance teams — not for lawyers.

## Property and BBMP terms

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **Khata** | BBMP's account of a property for tax and identification: owner liable for tax, property number, dimensions, use. Not a title document. Comes as a Khata certificate (existence, owner) and a Khata extract (details). |
| **A Khata** | Khata in the main register, for properties complying with bye-laws and approved layouts. Needed for plan sanction, most bank loans and a clean sale. |
| **B Khata** | Entry in the "B register" for properties with irregularities (unapproved layout, no conversion, deviations). Taxed, but with restricted rights. Some are eligible for conversion to A Khata. |
| **e-Khata** | The digital Khata issued through BBMP's e-Aasthi system, with a property identifier. Now required for registration of property within BBMP limits. |
| **e-Aasthi** | BBMP's online property record and e-Khata platform, where owners search, verify and apply for their digital Khata. |
| **EPID** | The e-Khata property identification number assigned on e-Aasthi, used in applications such as Khata conversion. |
| **Khata transfer / mutation** | Updating the Khata to the new owner after sale, gift, inheritance, partition or release. Different from registration of the deed. |
| **Khata bifurcation / amalgamation** | Splitting one Khata into several (units of a building, divided sites, heirs) or merging adjacent properties into one. |
| **Encumbrance Certificate (EC)** | Sub-registrar's certificate listing registered transactions (sales, mortgages, releases) on a property for a period. Obtained via Kaveri Online Services or the office. |
| **RTC / Pahani** | Record of Rights, Tenancy and Crops — the revenue record for agricultural land, showing ownership and cultivation. |
| **DC conversion** | Deputy Commissioner's order converting agricultural land to non-agricultural use; required before layout approval, sanction and A Khata. |
| **Guidance value** | The government's minimum value for a property, on which stamp duty and registration fees are computed. |
| **Plan sanction** | BBMP/BDA approval of a building plan under the bye-laws, required before construction. |
| **Occupancy certificate (OC)** | Certificate after completion that the building conforms to the sanctioned plan and is fit for occupation. |
| **SAS** | Self-Assessment Scheme for BBMP property tax: owners declare area and use and pay accordingly; under-declaration attracts penalty. |
| **BDA / BMRDA / BIAPPA** | Bangalore Development Authority; Bangalore Metropolitan Region Development Authority; Bangalore International Airport Area Planning Authority — planning authorities for areas outside or overlapping BBMP. |
| **Power of attorney (POA)** | Document authorising someone to act for the owner; for NRIs, executed abroad and adjudicated/registered in Karnataka. |

## GST terms

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **GSTIN** | The 15-character GST registration number of a business in a state. |
| **GSTR-1 / GSTR-3B** | Return of outward supplies / summary return with tax payment, filed monthly or quarterly. |
| **GSTR-2B** | Auto-drafted statement of input tax credit available for a period, based on suppliers' filings; ITC is effectively restricted to it. |
| **GSTR-9 / 9C** | Annual return / reconciliation statement with audited financials above the turnover limit. |
| **ITC** | Input tax credit — GST paid on purchases, set off against GST on sales, subject to conditions. |
| **QRMP** | Quarterly Return, Monthly Payment scheme for smaller taxpayers. |
| **ASMT-10** | Notice of discrepancies found on scrutiny of returns; reply (ASMT-11) within the period stated. |
| **DRC-01A** | Intimation of tax ascertained before a show-cause notice; pay or respond. |
| **DRC-01 / SCN** | Show-cause notice under section 73 (non-fraud) or 74 (fraud/suppression) proposing a demand; reply (DRC-06) and hearing follow. |
| **APL-01** | First appeal to the appellate authority against an order, within three months, with pre-deposit. |
| **Pre-deposit** | Admitted tax plus a prescribed percentage of disputed tax, paid to file an appeal; balance recovery is stayed. |
| **Reverse charge (RCM)** | Cases where the recipient, not the supplier, pays GST. |
| **E-invoice / e-way bill** | Mandatory electronic invoicing above the turnover threshold; electronic document for movement of goods above the value limit. |

Terms are explained for orientation; the law and BBMP/GST procedures change. For your case, [ask us](https://www.marvelconsultants.co.in/contact/).

# How we work: from first message to closed file

> What happens after you contact Marvel Consultants: free first assessment, a written scope and fixed fee, the documents we need, how filing and follow-up work, how you get updates, and what we do not do. Bengaluru property, BBMP and GST matters.

Source: https://www.marvelconsultants.co.in/how-we-work/  ·  Organisation: Marvel Consultants, Bengaluru  ·  Phone: +91 91875 98642  ·  WhatsApp: https://wa.me/919187598642  ·  Last reviewed: 2026-08-29

No mystery about the process. This is what an engagement looks like, start to finish.

1. **You tell us** — WhatsApp, call or the form. Describe what you are trying to do or what went wrong. Photos of your documents help; originals are not needed yet.
2. **We assess — free** — We check the official records where possible and reply, usually the same working day, with what applies, what is missing and whether you can do it yourself.
3. **Scope and fee** — If you want us to handle it: a short written scope, a fixed professional fee, and the list of documents and government fees. You approve before work starts.
4. **We execute** — Preparation, filing, office attendance, replies to queries, and follow-up. You receive photographs of acknowledgements and a status note at each step.
5. **Closure** — The certificate, order, approval or reply — and a note of anything to keep, renew or do next.

## Fees

Fixed professional fees, quoted after assessment, per matter (or monthly for ongoing GST compliance; per stage or per unit for projects). Government fees, stamp duty, betterment charges, pre-deposits and statutory levies are paid to the authority and are always separate. We do not charge "facilitation" or unexplained expenses.

## What we need from you

- Documents as scans or photos to start; originals only when an office requires them
- A decision-maker we can reach for approvals and signatures
- Honesty about the history — an undisclosed deviation or dispute costs more later
- For NRIs: a power of attorney, which we help you set up

## What we do not do

- Guarantee approvals, timelines or outcomes that depend on an authority
- Title opinions, litigation or court representation (we refer to advocates and work alongside them)
- Statutory audit or certification reserved to chartered accountants / company secretaries (we coordinate with yours)
- Anything that involves misrepresenting facts to an authority

## Communication

WhatsApp and phone during working hours, email for documents and formal notes. Calls scheduled for NRI clients' time zones. Every filing is acknowledged with a photograph or portal reference.

## Frequently asked questions

**Q: Do I need to visit your office to start?**

A: No. Most matters start with a call or WhatsApp and photographs of your documents. We meet at our Yeshwanthpur office or at the property when a physical inspection, signature or original document is needed.

**Q: How are your fees structured?**

A: A fixed professional fee agreed before work starts, quoted after a free first assessment of your documents. Government fees, stamp duty and statutory charges are separate and paid to the authority. We do not quote a headline price for complex matters because the work depends on what the records show.

**Q: Can you guarantee the approval or the timeline?**

A: No, and you should be wary of anyone who does. Approvals rest with BBMP, BDA, the sub-registrar or the GST department. What we control is a complete, correct application, follow-up with the office, and honest communication about where it stands.

# BBMP B-Khata to A-Khata Conversion Bangalore 2026 | Marvel Consultants

> Convert your Bangalore property from B-Khata to A-Khata under the 2026 GBA scheme. Eligibility, documents, fees & step-by-step process. Free consult: +91 91875 98642

Source: https://www.marvelconsultants.co.in/bbmp/b-khata-to-a-khata-conversion/  ·  Organisation: Marvel Consultants, Bengaluru  ·  Phone: +91 91875 98642  ·  WhatsApp: https://wa.me/919187598642

If you own an independent house or a vacant plot in Bangalore that is currently registered under B-Khata, 2026 is the most cost-effective year in over a decade to convert it to A-Khata. Under the Greater Bengaluru Authority's (GBA) 100-Day Special Drive, running from 16 May 2026 to 23 August 2026, the government has temporarily reduced the betterment/conversion charge to just 2% of the guidance value. Outside this window, the same conversion can cost significantly more.

At [Marvel Consultants](https://www.marvelconsultants.co.in/index.html), we've spent over 10 years helping Bengaluru property owners and business owners navigate BBMP and GST paperwork without the runaround. This guide walks you through exactly what B-Khata and A-Khata mean, who qualifies for conversion, what documents you need, and how the online and offline processes work — so you can decide whether to act before the window closes.

Already dealing with a GST notice on the same property or business? See how we help with [GST compliance and dispute resolution](https://www.marvelconsultants.co.in/gst.html), or read our step-by-step breakdown of [what to do when you receive a GST notice](https://www.marvelconsultants.co.in/gst.html).

#### GBA 100-Day Special Drive (16 May – 23 Aug 2026)

Betterment/conversion charges reduced to **2% of guidance value**. Applications after 23 Aug 2026 may revert to a higher fee structure.

## What Is the Difference Between A-Khata and B-Khata?

A Khata is BBMP's record of a property for tax and identification purposes — it is not a title document, but it is required for nearly every civic and financial transaction involving the property. A-Khata is issued to properties that fully comply with BBMP's building bye-laws and approved layouts. B-Khata is a secondary register for properties with minor irregularities — such as unapproved layouts, pending conversion orders, or deviations — which are still taxed but carry restricted rights.

If your site originally came from a Panchayat or BDA layout, it helps to understand which authority's records actually govern your property — see our comparison of [BDA vs BBMP Khata](https://www.marvelconsultants.co.in/blog/bda-khata-transfer-guide.html) for clarity before you apply.

### A-Khata vs B-Khata — Quick Comparison

## Why Convert to A-Khata Now

- Home loans and mortgages become available — most banks will not lend against a B-Khata property.
- Higher resale value and a wider pool of buyers, since most purchasers and their banks prefer A-Khata.
- Eligibility for [building plan approvals](https://www.marvelconsultants.co.in/bbmp.html), renovation permits, and completion certificates.
- Stronger legal standing against future disputes or demolition action.
- Access to full civic services — BWSSB water connection, BBMP drainage, and related amenities.
- Eligibility to apply for BBMP trade licences if you plan to run a business from the property.
Planning to formalise a business at this address once your Khata is upgraded? Our [GST audit checklist for small businesses in Karnataka](https://www.marvelconsultants.co.in/gst-audit-compliance-bengaluru.html) is a useful next read.

## Who Can Apply for B-Khata to A-Khata Conversion

#### &#9989; Eligibility Criteria (2026 GBA Scheme)

- You hold a valid B-Khata, or a final E-Khata with an EPID.
- The property was registered on or before 30 September 2024.
- All property tax dues are fully cleared, with no pending arrears.
- The property is an independent house or a vacant plot/site — not a flat in a multi-unit apartment.
- The property has direct access to a public road.
- Both converted sites (holding a DC conversion order) and unconverted revenue sites can apply, though unconverted sites attract additional charges.
- Plots up to 2,000 sq. m. can apply through self-application; larger plots require a registered architect or engineer.

#### &#10060; Who Cannot Apply

- Flat owners in apartments or multi-storey buildings with multiple unit owners.
- Properties without a final E-Khata or EPID.
- Properties with major, unregularised building violations or encroachments.
- Properties registered after 30 September 2024.
If your land was originally Panchayat or revenue land, our [Panchayat to BBMP Khata conversion guide](https://www.marvelconsultants.co.in/blog/panchayat-khata-guide.html) covers this route in detail.

Own the property but currently live outside India? Our [NRI property management guide](https://www.marvelconsultants.co.in/bbmp.html) covers how to handle Khata conversion and GST matters remotely.

Not sure which category your property falls under? [Book a free 15-minute consultation](https://www.marvelconsultants.co.in/contact.html) with Marvel Consultants and we'll check your eligibility before you spend a single rupee on the application.

### Not sure if your property qualifies?

Get a free 15-minute eligibility check before you spend anything on the application.

## Documents You Will Need

- Registered sale deed / title deed of the property
- Aadhaar card for all owners (linked for OTP-based E-KYC)
- Latest property tax receipts showing nil dues
- Existing B-Khata / E-Khata certificate with EPID
- Latest BESCOM electricity bill as address proof
- Site plan / building sketch prepared by a licensed architect or engineer
- Recent photographs of the property
- DC conversion order, if the land was previously agricultural
- Encumbrance Certificate (EC) confirming no pending loans or disputes — if you're unsure why this document matters, our [Sale Deed & Encumbrance Certificate guide](https://www.marvelconsultants.co.in/bbmp.html) explains it in plain language.

## How the Online Application Works

- Log in to the BBMP portalLog in to BBMP's official Khata conversion portal using your mobile number and OTP.
- Raise a new requestRaise a new request and enter your existing E-Khata EPID to auto-fetch your property details.
- Complete Aadhaar E-KYCComplete Aadhaar E-KYC for every listed owner — an Application ID is generated once this is done.
- Confirm property locationConfirm your property's exact location on the map, since BBMP's inspection team will visit this pinned location.
- Declare revenue survey statusDeclare whether the property sits on a revenue survey number and upload the DC conversion order if you have one.
- Upload documentsUpload the full document set — sale deed, tax receipts, site sketch, and photographs — and self-certify eligibility.
- Pay the application feePay the &#8377;500 application fee online and download your acknowledgement slip.
- Ground inspectionBBMP conducts a physical ground inspection of the property.
- Pay conversion fee & receive A-KhataOn approval, pay the conversion fee (2% of guidance value under the current drive) and receive your digital A-Khata certificate.

## How the Offline Application Works

- Confirm eligibilityConfirm eligibility — valid B-Khata, cleared taxes, road access, and no major violations.
- Collect the formVisit your jurisdictional ARO or BBMP zonal office and collect the Khata conversion form.
- Submit documentsSubmit the form with all supporting documents and applicable fees.
- Scrutiny & verificationBBMP scrutinises the documents and conducts a physical verification.
- Receive A-KhataOn approval, the A-Khata certificate is typically issued within 4–6 weeks.

## Conversion Fees — And Why the Timing Matters

#### Betterment/conversion charges reduced to 2% of guidance value

On a property with a &#8377;50 lakh guidance value, that is roughly &#8377;1,00,000 in conversion fees — a fraction of what similar regularisation schemes have historically charged. Applications submitted after 23 August 2026 may revert to a higher fee structure, so property owners who qualify have a genuine window to act.

Marvel Consultants' professional fee covers eligibility verification, full document preparation, portal filing, Aadhaar E-KYC coordination, guidance through both government payments, and follow-up with BBMP until your A-Khata certificate is in hand. ## Frequently Asked Questions

What is the difference between A-Khata and B-Khata?

A-Khata is BBMP's register for fully compliant properties with complete legal ownership recognition. B-Khata is a secondary register for properties with pending approvals or irregularities, which limits resale, mortgage, and construction rights.

Can flat owners apply for this conversion?

No. The 2026 GBA scheme applies only to independent houses and vacant plots. Owners of flats in multi-unit apartment buildings are not eligible under this process.

How long does the conversion take?

With complete documentation and no inspection issues, the online process typically takes 30–60 days. Offline applications through a BBMP office may take 4–6 weeks after verification.

What happens if I don't have a DC conversion order?

You can still apply. BBMP levies additional charges for unconverted revenue or agricultural land, but the application itself is not rejected on this basis alone.

Is clearing property tax dues mandatory before applying?

Yes — this is a non-negotiable requirement. Keep your latest paid tax receipts ready to upload with your application.

Eligibility verification, document preparation and review, portal filing, Aadhaar E-KYC coordination, payment guidance, and continuous follow-up with BBMP until your A-Khata certificate is issued. Government fees are paid separately, directly to BBMP.

## How to Apply for BBMP E-Khata Online – Step-by-Step Process

Follow these steps to apply online for your BBMP e-Khata via the official e-Aasthi portal:

- Visit the official **BBMP e-Aasthi portal** at [bbmpeaasthi.karnataka.gov.in](https://bbmpeaasthi.karnataka.gov.in).
- Log in with your registered mobile number, or sign up if you are a first-time user.
- Search your property using the **PID or EPID number** issued by BBMP.
- Upload required documents — Aadhaar, sale deed, encumbrance certificate, latest tax receipt and property photographs.
- Pay the **mutation fee online (2% of stamp duty paid at registration, minimum ₹500)**.
- Track your application — this is the simple **e-Khata status check** tool on the portal using your reference number.
- Once verified by the Assistant Revenue Officer (ARO), download your verified **e-Khata for ₹125**.

## B-Khata to A-Khata Conversion — Get Your E-Khata Regularised

A **B-Khata** is issued to properties with pending approvals, deviations from sanctioned plans, or land that has not been formally regularised. While B-Khata lets you pay property tax, it is not accepted by banks for home loans and is not treated as a title deed during property sales.

Under the Government of Karnataka's **November 2025 regularisation drive**, B-Khata holders can now apply online via the BBMP e-Aasthi portal to convert their record to a Final A-Khata. This **B-Khata to A-Khata conversion in Bengaluru** requires clearing outstanding property tax dues, paying applicable Betterment Charges (typically 0.5% to 1.5% of land value), and ensuring proper DC conversion is in place.

Marvel Consultants handles the full **B-Khata e-Khata conversion** end-to-end — from Betterment Charge calculation to portal filing and ARO verification — so your property receives a clean, lendable A-Khata title.

A Draft e-Khata is an auto-generated digital record of your property based on legacy data. It is a pre-verified document that acts as a starting point for digitization but carries no legal weight for property sales or bank loans.

The Final e-Khata is the mandatory digital certificate for property owners in Bengaluru. It is a secure, QR-coded document required for:

- **Legal Transactions:** Buying or selling property.
- **Financial Approvals:** Applying for home loans or mortgages.
- **Permissions:** Securing building plan sanctions and electricity connections.

- **e-KYC:** Link your Aadhaar and contact details to the property record.
- **Document Upload:** Submit your registered sale deed and the latest tax receipts.
- **Verification:** Once the Assistant Revenue Officer (ARO) verifies your documents, the status is updated from "Draft" to "Final."
- **A-Khata:** Issued to properties that are fully compliant with all building bylaws and have clear land titles.

## How to Convert B Khata to A Khata in Bangalore: Complete Guide to Fees, Documents & Process (2026)

Property ownership documentation plays a crucial role in Bangalore's real estate market. One of the most common concerns among property owners is converting a **B Khata property to an A Khata property**. With the latest government initiatives and simplified online procedures, converting your property has become easier than ever.

At **Marvel Consultants**, we assist property owners across Bangalore with [Khata Transfer](https://www.marvelconsultants.co.in/blog/khata-transfer-guide.html), B Khata to A Khata Conversion, [E-Khata Registration](https://www.marvelconsultants.co.in/blog/e-khata-online-bangalore-karnataka-complete-guide.html), Property Documentation, and Legal Verification Services.

#### Quick Summary (2026)

Converting B Khata to A Khata in Bangalore now costs approximately **2% of the guidance value** (reduced from 5%), can be done **online via the BBMP e-Aasthi portal**, and typically takes **30–45 days**. Read on for the full eligibility, documents, fees and step-by-step process.

## What is B Khata?

A **B Khata** is a property record maintained by BBMP for properties that do not fully comply with zoning regulations, building bye-laws, or land conversion norms. While owners can pay property tax under B Khata, the property is **not considered fully regularized**.

Common reasons for B Khata classification include:

- Properties built on revenue land
- Unapproved layouts
- Deviations from sanctioned building plans
- Missing land conversion documents
- Properties with legal compliance issues

## What is A Khata?

An **A Khata** is an official BBMP property record issued to legally compliant properties. It confirms that the property follows municipal regulations and is eligible for various civic and financial benefits.

Benefits of A Khata include:

- &#10004; Easy Home Loan Approval
- &#10004; Higher Property Resale Value
- &#10004; Building Plan Approval
- &#10004; Smooth Property Registration
- &#10004; Legal Ownership Recognition
- &#10004; Better Investment Opportunities

## Difference Between A Khata and B Khata

## Why Convert B Khata to A Khata?

Converting your property offers several advantages:

#### 1. Easier Loan Approvals

Banks and financial institutions prefer A Khata properties for housing loans.

#### 2. Increased Property Value

A Khata properties attract more buyers and command better market prices.

#### 3. Legal Security

It strengthens your ownership rights and reduces future legal complications.

#### 4. Building Plan Sanctions

BBMP generally approves construction and renovation plans only for A Khata properties.

#### 5. Smooth Property Transactions

Selling, gifting, or transferring an A Khata property is much easier.

## Documents Required for B Khata to A Khata Conversion

- Registered Sale Deed

- Latest Electricity Bill
- Water Bill
- Property Sketch
- Passport Size Photograph

### Additional Documents (If Applicable)

- DC Conversion Order
- Approved Building Plan
- Occupancy Certificate

#### Pro Tip

Keep both physical and scanned (PDF) copies ready. Clear, legible scans speed up online verification on the BBMP e-Aasthi portal and reduce the chance of rejection.

## Eligibility for B Khata to A Khata Conversion

Before applying, ensure that:

- Property taxes are fully paid
- Property has clear ownership records
- Land conversion has been completed (if applicable)
- Property has proper road access

- Zoning regulations are complied with

## Step-by-Step Process for B Khata to A Khata Conversion in Bangalore

### Offline Process

- Step 1: Verify Eligibility Check whether your property qualifies for conversion under BBMP regulations.
- Step 2: Clear Outstanding Dues Pay all pending taxes and penalties.
- Step 3: Collect Application Form Visit the concerned BBMP office or Assistant Revenue Officer (ARO) office.
- Step 4: Submit Documents Attach all supporting documents and submit the application.
- Step 5: Pay Applicable Fees Pay the application fee and conversion charges.
- Step 6: Property Inspection BBMP officials may conduct site verification.
- Step 7: Approval and Issuance Upon approval, the A Khata certificate will be issued.

### Online Process Through the BBMP e-Aasthi Portal

- Step 1: Visit the Portal Visit the official BBMP e-Aasthi portal.
- Step 2: Locate Your Property Find your property using the PID Number, ePID Number, Assessment Number or Ward Number.
- Step 3: Upload Documents Upload all required documents.
- Step 4: Aadhaar e-KYC Complete Aadhaar e-KYC verification.
- Step 5: Pay the Application Fee Pay the application fee online.
- Step 6: Verification & Inspection Await verification and inspection by BBMP officials.
- Step 7: Pay Betterment Charges Pay betterment charges if applicable.
- Step 8: Receive A Khata Certificate Receive your A Khata certificate online.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

1. How much does B Khata to A Khata conversion cost in Bangalore in 2026?

Under the latest government initiative, conversion charges are approximately **2% of the property's guidance value** (reduced from 5% earlier), plus a nominal application fee of around &#8377;500, a Khata certificate fee of &#8377;25 and a Khata extract fee of &#8377;100. Betterment and DC conversion charges may apply depending on the property.

2. How long does B Khata to A Khata conversion take?

On average the process takes about **30 to 45 days** (roughly 4 to 6 weeks), depending on document verification and site inspection timelines.

3. What documents are required for B Khata to A Khata conversion?

You need the registered sale deed, current B Khata certificate, khata extract, latest property tax receipts, Aadhaar card, encumbrance certificate, latest electricity and water bills, property sketch and a passport-size photograph. DC conversion order, approved building plan, occupancy certificate and betterment charge receipts may be required if applicable.

4. Can I convert B Khata to A Khata online in Bangalore?

Yes. You can apply through the official **BBMP e-Aasthi portal** by locating your property with the PID or assessment number, uploading documents, completing Aadhaar e-KYC, paying the fees online and receiving your A Khata certificate after verification.

5. Why is A Khata better than B Khata?

An A Khata confirms your property is legally compliant. It enables easy home loan approval, higher resale value, building plan sanctions, smooth property registration and full legal ownership recognition, whereas a B Khata offers only semi-legal status with limited loan and approval options.

6. Why do conversion applications get rejected?

Common reasons include incomplete documentation, outstanding property tax arrears, ownership disputes or court cases, zoning and land-use violations, lack of proper public road access, and unapproved layouts.

## What Is the Difference Between A-Khata and B-Khata?

A Khata is BBMP's record of a property for tax and identification purposes — it is not a title document, but it is required for nearly every civic and financial transaction involving the property. A-Khata is issued to properties that fully comply with BBMP's building bye-laws and approved layouts. B-Khata is a secondary register for properties with minor irregularities — such as unapproved layouts, pending conversion orders, or deviations — which are still taxed but carry restricted rights.

# Complete Guide to BDA Khata Transfer in Bangalore | Marvel Consultants

> Get complete information on BDA Khata transfer in Bangalore. Learn about the process, fees, and how to apply online for hassle-free khata transfer services.

Source: https://www.marvelconsultants.co.in/blog/bda-khata-transfer-guide.html  ·  Organisation: Marvel Consultants, Bengaluru  ·  Phone: +91 91875 98642  ·  WhatsApp: https://wa.me/919187598642

## BDA Khata Transfer: A Complete Guide

A BDA (Bangalore Development Authority) Khata is a crucial document that officially records property ownership for properties falling under BDA jurisdiction in Bangalore. Unlike properties managed by BBMP (Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike), BDA properties have a separate Khata system administered by the Bangalore Development Authority.

The BDA Khata serves as a comprehensive record that contains vital information about your property including dimensions, location, built-up area, property usage, and ownership details. This document is essential for various purposes such as property tax payments, property transactions, loan applications, and obtaining construction permissions.

#### Why This Guide Matters

Understanding the BDA Khata transfer process is crucial for property owners in Bangalore. This guide demystifies the process and helps you navigate through the various requirements to ensure your property ownership is legally recognized by the BDA.

## Importance of BDA Khata

The BDA Khata is more than just a document - it's the official recognition of your property ownership for properties under BDA jurisdiction. Here's why it holds significant importance:

#### Legal Proof of Ownership

The Khata serves as an official record that establishes your legal ownership of the property in the eyes of the Bangalore Development Authority.

#### Property Tax Payments

It enables you to pay property taxes to the BDA, ensuring compliance with local revenue regulations.

#### Property Transactions

A valid Khata is necessary for selling, purchasing, or transferring property ownership within BDA limits.

#### Loan Applications

Financial institutions require the Khata certificate as proof of ownership when processing loan applications against the property.

#### Utility Connections

Obtaining water, electricity, or other utility connections requires a valid Khata certificate.

Without a properly transferred Khata, you may face various legal and administrative challenges that could affect your property rights and transactions in Bangalore.

## When Is BDA Khata Transfer Required?

BDA Khata transfer becomes necessary in several situations. Understanding these scenarios will help you initiate the transfer process at the appropriate time:

#### Important Note

It's advisable to initiate the Khata transfer process as soon as the property ownership changes. Delaying the process may lead to complications in property tax payments and future transactions.

## Documents Required for BDA Khata Transfer

The documentation process is a critical aspect of BDA Khata transfer. Ensure you have the following documents ready before initiating the application:

- **Sale Deed or Title Document:** The registered document that proves the transfer of property ownership.
- **Previous Khata Extract:** The existing Khata extract in the seller's name.
- **Encumbrance Certificate:** A document that confirms there are no legal claims or liabilities against the property.
- **Property Tax Receipts:** Proof of property tax payments up to the current financial year.
- **BDA Allotment Letter:** If the property was directly allotted by BDA.
- **Identity Proof:** Aadhaar card, voter ID, or passport of the new owner.
- **Address Proof:** Document proving the residential address of the new owner.
- **Photographs:** Passport-sized photographs of the new property owner.
- **NOC from Previous Owner:** No Objection Certificate from the previous owner (in some cases).
- **Possession Certificate:** Document showing legal possession of the property.

#### Document Verification

All documents should be self-attested, and you may need to produce original documents for verification at the BDA office.

## Step-by-Step BDA Khata Transfer Process

The BDA Khata transfer process involves several steps that need to be followed meticulously. Here's a comprehensive guide to help you navigate through the process:

- Document Collection Gather all the required documents mentioned in the previous section. Ensure that all documents are complete, valid, and properly attested.
- Application Form Obtain the Khata transfer application form from the BDA office or download it from the official BDA website. Fill it with accurate details about the property and new ownership information.
- Payment of Fees Pay the prescribed Khata transfer fee at the BDA office. The fee amount varies depending on the property value and other factors, typically ranging from 2% to 5% of the guidance value.
- Submission of Application Submit the completed application form along with all supporting documents and fee receipt to the designated BDA officer.
- Field Verification The BDA officials may conduct a field visit to verify the property details mentioned in your application.
- Application Processing The application undergoes scrutiny and processing by the BDA officials. This may involve cross-verification with land records and property tax registers.
- Approval and Issuance After successful verification, the BDA approves the Khata transfer and issues a new Khata certificate and extract in the new owner's name.

#### Processing Time

The entire process typically takes 30-45 days, depending on the workload at the BDA office and the complexity of your case.

## Common Challenges and Solutions

Several challenges may arise during the BDA Khata transfer process. Being aware of these challenges and their solutions can help you navigate the process more effectively:

#### Incomplete Documentation

**Challenge:** Missing or incomplete documents can delay the process.

**Solution:** Prepare a comprehensive checklist of required documents and verify each document's completeness before submission.

#### Property Tax Dues

**Challenge:** Pending property tax payments can hinder the Khata transfer.

**Solution:** Ensure all property taxes are paid up to date before applying for the transfer. Request tax payment history from the BDA.

#### Discrepancies in Property Details

**Challenge:** Differences between actual property details and records can cause complications.

**Solution:** Conduct a thorough verification of property records and address any discrepancies before initiating the Khata transfer process.

#### Bureaucratic Delays

**Challenge:** Administrative delays at the BDA level can prolong the process.

**Solution:** Maintain regular follow-ups with the BDA officials and keep track of your application status.

#### Ownership Disputes

**Challenge:** Disputes regarding property ownership can halt the transfer process.

**Solution:** Resolve any ownership disputes through legal channels before applying for Khata transfer.

## Tips for a Smooth BDA Khata Transfer

Follow these practical tips to ensure a hassle-free BDA Khata transfer experience:

- **Start Early:** Initiate the transfer process as soon as the property ownership changes to avoid complications.
- **Keep Organized Records:** Maintain multiple copies of all documents in an organized manner for easy reference.
- **Seek Professional Guidance:** Consider hiring a property consultant familiar with BDA procedures to assist you through the process.
- **Be Present for Verification:** Try to be personally present during the field verification to address any queries on the spot.
- **Build Rapport:** Establish a cordial relationship with BDA officials to facilitate smoother processing.
- **Digital Copies:** Keep digital scans of all documents for backup and easy sharing when needed.
- **Track Application:** Maintain a record of your application number and submission date for follow-ups.
- **Clear Property Tax Dues:** Ensure all property taxes are paid before applying for the transfer.

#### Professional Assistance

If you find the process overwhelming, consider hiring a property consultant or lawyer who specializes in BDA property matters. They can guide you through the process and handle documentation on your behalf.

## Differences Between BDA and BBMP Khata

Understanding the differences between BDA Khata and BBMP Khata can help property owners in Bangalore navigate the process more effectively:

It's important to note that some properties in Bangalore might need both BDA and BBMP Khata, depending on their location and development history.

## Legal Aspects of BDA Khata

It's important to understand the legal implications and aspects of BDA Khata to avoid future complications:

#### Not a Title Document

A Khata certificate is not a title document but rather a fiscal document for property tax assessment. It doesn't guarantee ownership in case of disputes.

#### Tax Liability

The person whose name appears on the Khata is legally responsible for paying property taxes to the BDA.

#### BDA Layout Regulations

Properties with BDA Khata must comply with BDA layout regulations and zoning requirements.

#### Statutory Requirements

The BDA Khata process is governed by the BDA Act and related regulations, and compliance with these legal provisions is mandatory.

#### Legal Consultation

For properties with complex ownership history or ongoing disputes, it's advisable to consult with a property lawyer before initiating the Khata transfer process.

# BBMP E Khata Complete Guide | Marvel Consultants

> Property documentation is an important part of owning, selling, transferring, or developing a property in Bangalore. With the digitization of property…

Source: https://www.marvelconsultants.co.in/blog/e-aasthi-a-khata-b-khata-conversion.html  ·  Organisation: Marvel Consultants, Bengaluru  ·  Phone: +91 91875 98642  ·  WhatsApp: https://wa.me/919187598642

August 25, 2026 | E-Khata Guide

Property documentation is an important part of owning, selling, transferring, or developing a property in Bangalore. With the digitization of property records, **BBMP E Khata** and **BBMP E Aasthi** have become important terms for property owners.

The **Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike (BBMP)** has introduced digital systems to make property records easier to access and manage. A Khata record contains important information related to property ownership, identification, taxation, and other property details.

Property owners commonly search for information about **BBMP E Khata, BBMP E Aasthi, A Khata, B Khata, B Khata to A Khata conversion, and Khata bifurcation** when they need to update or regularize their property records.

This guide explains the basics of BBMP E Khata, the difference between A Khata and B Khata, the conversion process, required documents, Khata bifurcation, and common issues faced by property owners.

## What is BBMP E Aasthi (BBMP E Khata)?

**BBMP E Aasthi** refers to the digital property record system through which property-related information can be maintained electronically. BBMP E Khata provides a digital representation of property records that were traditionally maintained through physical Khata documents.

The digital record can contain information such as:

- Property identification details
- Owner information
- Property tax information
- Property measurements and details
- Khata-related information
- Other applicable property records
The digitization of property records can make it easier for property owners to access and manage their information.

### Benefits of BBMP E Khata

Some of the key benefits of maintaining updated digital property records include:

- Easier access to property information
- Convenient property tax-related processes
- Better record management
- Reduced dependency on physical documents
- Easier verification of property information
- Support for property-related transactions and applications, subject to applicable rules
Property owners should ensure that the information recorded in their digital property records is accurate and matches their supporting documents.

## Understanding A Khata and B Khata

One of the most common questions among Bangalore property owners is the difference between **A Khata and B Khata**.

### What is A Khata?

An **A Khata** generally refers to a property record associated with properties that meet the applicable municipal requirements and have the necessary approvals and documentation.

Depending on the property and applicable regulations, A Khata properties may have advantages such as:

- Better eligibility for property-related transactions
- Easier access to certain financial services
- Better resale prospects
- Ability to apply for applicable building permissions
- Improved documentation status
However, having an A Khata does not by itself replace the need to verify title, approvals, land-use permissions, and other legal requirements.

### What is B Khata?

A **B Khata** generally refers to properties recorded separately for taxation purposes where there may be deviations, incomplete approvals, or other issues affecting the property&#39;s compliance status.

A B Khata property may face limitations depending on the nature of the issue, including:

- Difficulty obtaining certain approvals
- Challenges with some financial institutions
- Complications during property transactions
- Restrictions related to building permissions
- Difficulty regularizing or updating property records
Property owners should have their documents reviewed to understand the specific status of their property rather than relying only on the Khata category.

## Difference Between A Khata and B Khata

The exact legal position of a property depends on its documents, approvals, land status, and applicable regulations.

## BBMP B Khata to A Khata Conversion

Many property owners want to convert their **B Khata to A Khata** to improve their property&#39;s documentation and compliance status.

However, conversion is not automatic. The property&#39;s eligibility depends on several factors, including the property documents, land status, approvals, building compliance, and applicable government regulations.

### General Steps for B Khata to A Khata Conversion

The process may generally involve the following steps:

### 1. Verify Property Documents

The first step is to review the available property documents and identify any discrepancies, missing documents, or compliance issues.

Documents may include:

- Sale deed
- Previous title documents
- Property tax receipts
- Encumbrance Certificate
- Khata documents
- Building plan or approval documents
- Identity and address proof
- Other applicable property documents

### 2. Check Property and Building Compliance

The property should be examined for applicable land, building, planning, and municipal requirements.

Any deviation or missing approval should be identified before proceeding.

### 3. Clear Outstanding Property Taxes

Pending property taxes and other applicable dues should be checked and cleared as required.

### 4. Submit the Application

Once the property documents and eligibility are verified, the applicable application for Khata conversion can be submitted along with the required supporting documents.

### 5. Pay Applicable Charges

Depending on the property and applicable rules, the owner may need to pay applicable conversion, betterment, regularization, or other charges.

### 6. Verification and Processing

The submitted documents and property details may be reviewed by the concerned authority.

If discrepancies are identified, additional documents or corrections may be required.

### 7. Updated Khata Record

After successful processing and approval, the property&#39;s Khata record may be updated according to the applicable process.

Because requirements can vary depending on the property, professional documentation assistance can help identify potential issues before submitting an application.

## Khata Bifurcation BBMP &mdash; When Is It Required?

**Khata bifurcation** refers to separating a property record into individual records when a property is divided or ownership is separated.

Khata bifurcation may be required in situations such as:

- Property inheritance
- Division among family members
- Joint property separation
- Plot subdivision
- Property partition
- Certain apartment or unit-related situations
After successful bifurcation, separate property records may be maintained for the respective properties or owners, subject to applicable rules and approvals.

### Why is Khata Bifurcation Important?

Khata bifurcation can help ensure that:

- Each property has appropriate individual records
- Property tax responsibilities are separated
- Ownership-related records are properly maintained
- Future property transactions are easier to document
- Individual property details can be maintained separately
The exact requirements depend on the type of property and reason for bifurcation.

## Why is BBMP Khata Important?

A properly maintained Khata record can be important for several property-related activities.

Property owners may need updated Khata documentation for processes such as:

- Property tax payment
- Property sale or purchase
- Property transfer
- Bank loan applications
- Building-related applications
- Property documentation
- Certain registration and municipal processes
However, Khata should not be considered the only document required to establish ownership or legal title. Property owners should also verify their sale deed, title documents, approvals, EC, and other applicable records.

## Documents Required for BBMP E Khata

The documents required may vary depending on the property and the type of application.

Common documents may include:

- Registered sale deed
- Previous title documents
- Property tax paid receipts
- Encumbrance Certificate (EC)
- Owner&#39;s identity proof
- Address proof
- Existing Khata certificate or extract, where applicable
- Property identification details
- Building plan or approval documents, where applicable
- Relevant conversion or sanction documents
- Other supporting documents requested by the concerned authority
For **B Khata to A Khata conversion**, additional documents may be required depending on the property&#39;s status and the reason for conversion.

Before applying, property owners should verify that the names, measurements, survey details, property numbers, and other information are consistent across the documents.

## Common Problems During BBMP E Khata Applications

Property owners may face several issues while applying for or updating digital Khata records.

Common problems include:

### Incorrect Property Details

The owner&#39;s name, property number, measurements, address, or other details may not match the supporting documents.

### Missing Documents

Applications can be delayed when required documents are unavailable or incomplete.

### Property Tax Issues

Outstanding taxes or discrepancies in tax records may need to be resolved before certain processes can proceed.

### Khata Bifurcation Issues

Bifurcation applications may require additional documentation when ownership or property boundaries are unclear.

### B Khata to A Khata Conversion Issues

Conversion may become complicated when there are building deviations, missing approvals, land-related issues, or other compliance concerns.

### Digital Record Errors

Errors in existing digital property records may need to be corrected through the applicable procedure.

Professional document verification before submitting an application can help reduce avoidable delays and errors.

## Frequently Asked Questions About BBMP E Khata

What is BBMP E Khata?

BBMP E Khata is the digital version of a property&#39;s Khata record maintained through the applicable BBMP digital property record system. It contains important property and tax-related information.

What is BBMP E Aasthi?

BBMP E Aasthi refers to the digital property record system used for maintaining and accessing property-related information electronically.

What is the difference between A Khata and B Khata?

A Khata generally relates to properties that meet applicable requirements and have the necessary approvals and documentation. B Khata may relate to properties with certain deviations, incomplete approvals, or other compliance issues.

Can B Khata be converted to A Khata?

B Khata to A Khata conversion may be possible for eligible properties depending on the property&#39;s documents, land status, approvals, building compliance, and applicable government rules. Each property needs to be assessed individually.

What documents are required for BBMP E Khata?

Common documents include the sale deed, property tax receipts, Encumbrance Certificate, identity proof, property details, and applicable building approval documents. Additional documents may be required depending on the application.

What is Khata bifurcation?

Khata bifurcation is the process of separating a property record into individual records when a property is divided, inherited, partitioned, or otherwise becomes eligible for separate records.

Why is BBMP E Khata important?

BBMP E Khata helps property owners maintain and access digital property records. Updated records can be useful for property tax, documentation, transactions, and other property-related processes.

Can mistakes in BBMP E Khata be corrected?

Property owners may be able to request corrections to errors in their digital property records through the applicable procedure. The documents required depend on the nature of the correction.

How long does BBMP E Khata processing take?

Processing time can vary depending on the application type, document verification, property records, corrections required, and the concerned authority&#39;s processing procedures.

Is Khata the same as property ownership proof?

No. Khata is an important municipal property record, but it should not be treated as a substitute for a registered title document. Property owners should verify the complete chain of title and other applicable legal documents.

Can professional consultants help with B Khata to A Khata conversion?

Yes. Professional consultants can help review property documents, identify potential documentation issues, prepare applicable paperwork, and provide assistance throughout the relevant process.

Where can I get assistance with BBMP E Khata?

Among these, **BBMP e Khata** and **BBMP e Aasthi** play a critical role in validating ownership, enabling property transfers, and supporting approvals for commercial activities. While the shift to digital systems was intended to simplify processes, many businesses still face delays due to avoidable e-Khata errors.

These mistakes can stall sales, delay loan approvals, impact lease agreements, and even disrupt project launches. For companies that rely on timely property documentation, such setbacks translate directly into financial losses and missed opportunities. Marvel Consultants helps businesses navigate e-Khata processes efficiently and without costly delays.

## Why e-Khata Is Crucial for Business Transactions

An **e-Khata** is the official digital record that establishes a property&rsquo;s legal standing with BBMP. It confirms that the property is registered, assessed, and recognized for taxation and administrative purposes. For businesses, e-Khata is commonly required for:

- Property purchase or sale
- Commercial lease registration
- Bank loans and mortgage approvals
- Building plan approvals and occupancy certificates
Without a valid and accurate e-Khata, transactions may be placed on hold, or worse, rejected. This makes e-Khata not just a compliance formality, but a foundation for smooth business operations.

## Common e-Khata Errors That Cause Delays

Understanding the most frequent mistakes can help property owners and businesses take preventive action.

### 1. Mismatch in Owner Details

Even small differences in spelling between sale deeds, Aadhaar, and previous khata records can result in rejection. Name order, initials, or missing middle names often trigger verification failures.

### 2. Incorrect Property Description

Plot size, boundaries, survey numbers, or apartment numbers that differ from earlier records create inconsistencies. BBMP systems cross-check these details automatically, and mismatches lead to objections.

### 3. Incomplete Supporting Documents

Missing sale deeds, tax receipts, occupancy certificates, or previous khata extracts are a common reason for applications being placed on hold.

### 4. Issues Related to b khata bbmp

Properties recorded under **b khata BBMP** frequently face challenges when migrating to e-Khata. If the property&rsquo;s status is unclear or supporting approvals are missing, the application may be rejected.

### 5. Problems with bbmp khata a khata bbmp Classification

When records are unclear about whether a property qualifies as A Khata, confusion arises. This directly affects eligibility for e-Khata.

### 6. Delays in bbmp b khata to a khata Conversion

Businesses that attempt **BBMP B Khata to A Khata** conversion without proper documentation often face prolonged scrutiny and repeated queries.

### 7. Errors in khata bifurcation bbmp

When a property is subdivided, each unit must have its own khata. Mistakes during **khata bifurcation BBMP** can prevent individual owners from obtaining e-Khata certificates.

### 8. Technical Upload Issues

Low-quality scans, missing pages, or incorrectly labeled files may cause digital rejection, even if documents are otherwise valid.

## How These Errors Impact Business Operations

- **Transaction Delays:** Property sales and leases are postponed.
- **Financing Issues:** Banks may withhold loan disbursement.
- **Project Slowdowns:** Building approvals get stuck.
- **Legal Risk:** Incomplete records increase dispute vulnerability.
For businesses operating on tight timelines, these risks can be damaging.

## Best Practices for Businesses Applying for e-Khata

- Ensure all names match across documents
- Use high-quality scanned copies
- Verify property measurements and boundaries
- Confirm khata classification before applying
- Seek professional review prior to submission
Following these steps reduces rejection risk and processing time.

## Why Outsourcing e-Khata Matters for Businesses

Handling e-Khata internally can be time-consuming and risky, especially for organizations without dedicated compliance teams.

- Faster processing
- Lower rejection rates
- Reduced compliance risk
- Peace of mind
For growing businesses, this allows focus on core operations while experts manage documentation.

BBMP e Aasthi is the online property database used to generate e-Khata and maintain ownership records.

## Complete Guide to E-Khata Online in Bangalore & Karnataka – Digital Property Records Explained

In the world of real estate, maintaining accurate property records and documentation is extremely important. In Karnataka, property management has become more transparent and convenient with the introduction of E Khata. It is the state's digital land record system that has replaced traditional paper-based property records. With BBMP E Khata online, property owners no longer need to depend on lengthy paperwork and manual processes.

This initiative is part of the Karnataka government's push toward digitalisation. Through E Khata online portals, property owners can easily manage and access their property records in a secure digital format.

E Khata provides a centralised online platform for property registration, tax payment, and ownership verification. This digital property record helps prevent fraud, speeds up transactions, and ensures easy access to property information for homeowners, buyers, and legal professionals.

Whether you want to apply for property documents, pay property tax, or verify ownership records, E Khata brings everything online and simplifies the entire process with secure and real-time updates.

#### Why This Guide Matters

E Khata is now mandatory for online building plan approvals in Karnataka from July 1, 2025. This comprehensive guide covers everything you need to know about obtaining your E Khata certificate online.

## Understanding E-Khata and Its Importance

BBMP E Khata is an electronic legal property document issued by the local municipal authority. E Khata is the digital version of the traditional Khata certificate and is managed by local bodies such as BBMP (Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike) in Bengaluru.

### What Exactly is E-Khata?

E Khata, often searched online as what is e khata or e khata online, is the digital format of the traditional Khata document issued for properties in Karnataka.

It contains complete digital records such as:

- Property ownership details
- Property tax payment history
- Transaction records
- Property identification information
E Khata serves as legal proof of property ownership and confirms that the property has received the necessary municipal approvals. Unlike physical records that are prone to errors or manipulation, E Khata is more secure, reliable, and tamper-proof.

#### Important Update

From July 1, 2025, submitting an E Khata is mandatory for online building plan approvals, including applications under the Nambike Nakshe scheme. This has made E Khata a key part of Karnataka's urban governance system.

E Khata ensures:

- Centralised digital records accessible anytime, anywhere
- Secure and tamper-proof documentation
- Real-time ownership updates
- Easy online property tax payments

## Why E-Khata is Important for Property Owners in Karnataka

E Khata is more than just a digital document — it plays a major role in modern property management. Here's why it is important:

#### Legal Validity

E Khata is required for property sales, bank loans, and mortgages. Most banks and financial institutions require it for verification.

#### Fraud Prevention

Digital records help eliminate fake documents and duplicate property entries.

#### Easy Transactions

Property owners can manage documentation online without visiting municipal offices.

#### Faster Approvals

Building plan approvals, registrations, and loan processing become quicker.

#### Transparency for Buyers

Buyers can verify property ownership before purchasing.

#### Supports Digital Governance

It contributes to India's digital transformation and smart governance initiatives.

#### Boosts Investor Confidence

Transparent records attract investors, developers, and home buyers in Bengaluru.

The introduction of E Khata has significantly improved the way property records and taxes are managed in Bengaluru and across Karnataka. Earlier, property owners had to visit BBMP offices multiple times for property registration or tax payments. Now, with E Khata, the entire process has become digital, faster, and more transparent.

## Step-by-Step E-Khata Application Process

Karnataka's E Khata system simplifies property documentation through digital records and online application procedures. Below is a complete guide to applying for E Khata online, including eligibility and required documents.

### Who is Eligible to Apply for E-Khata?

To apply for E Khata online, applicants must meet the following criteria:

- The property must fall under BBMP jurisdiction
- Applicable for residential, commercial, and industrial properties
Eligible applicants include:

- Property owners
- Joint owners
- Legal heirs
- Builders and developers
- Companies and LLPs
Applicants must be 18 years or older with a valid bank account.

#### Not Eligible for E-Khata

- Properties involved in legal disputes
- Unauthorized constructions
- Agricultural land (handled under RTC records)

## Required Documents for E-Khata Application

Before applying for E Khata online in Bengaluru, make sure you have the following documents.

### For BDA Allotted Sites / Flats

- Allotment Letter
- Lease-cum-Sale Deed / Sale Deed
- Possession Certificate
- Encumbrance Certificate (Form-15)
- Identity Proof
- Bank NOC (if the property has a loan)

### For BDA Approved Private Layout / Apartment

- Layout or Apartment Plan Approval
- Release Order
- Possession Certificate (if available)
- Allotment Letter (if available)
- Sale Deed / Lease-cum-Sale Deed
- Encumbrance Certificate
- ID Proof
- Society NOC (if applicable)
- Bank NOC (if property is under loan)

## How to Apply for E-Khata Online

Follow these steps to apply for an E Khata certificate:

- Visit the Seva Sindhu Karnataka Portal Go to the official Seva Sindhu Karnataka portal and click on Suvidha Services.
- Select BDA (Bangalore Development Authority) Choose Application for New E Khata. Read eligibility and fee details carefully.
- Register Using Your Aadhaar Number Complete the Aadhaar-based registration process to proceed with the application.
- Enter Property Details Fill in the required property details such as Property ID, Owner name, and Property size.
- Upload Required Documents Upload all the necessary documents as listed in the requirements section.
- Complete E-Sign Verification Verify your identity through the e-sign process.
- Review and Submit Review all the details carefully and submit the application. You will receive an acknowledgement number. Verification usually takes up to 15 days.

#### Pro Tip

Once approved, you can download your digitally signed E Khata certificate from the portal.

## How to Check Your E-Khata Status Online

If you have applied for E Khata, you can easily track your application.

### Steps to Check Status

- Visit the Seva Sindhu portal.
- Select your preferred language.
- Click Track Application Status.
- Enter your application number.
- View your application status.

### Possible Application Status

## How to Download Your E-Khata Certificate

Downloading your E Khata certificate is the final step of the registration process.

### Why You Need the E-Khata Certificate

It is required for:

- Buying or selling property
- Applying for home loans
- Property tax payments
- Legal dispute resolution
- Utility connections like water or electricity

### Steps to Download E-Khata

- Log in to the Seva Sindhu Portal Access the portal using your registered credentials.
- Check Application Status Verify that your application has been approved.
- Go to Issue Document Once approved, navigate to the Issue Document section.
- Click Output Certificate Select the Output Certificate option to generate your E Khata.
- Download the E Khata PDF Download and save the PDF. Always verify the details such as property information, owner name, digital seal and signature.

## Common Issues During E-Khata Application

Although the process is online, some users may face issues such as:

#### Missing Documents

Incomplete document submission during the application process.

#### Website Technical Errors

Slow portal response or technical errors on the website.

#### Delay in Status Updates

Application status may take time to reflect changes.

#### Incorrect Property Details

Errors in property information entered during application.

#### Pending Property Tax Dues

Outstanding tax payments can block the application.

#### Tips to Avoid Delays

- Double-check all documents before uploading
- Apply during non-peak hours
- Clear pending taxes
- Ensure correct property details
If problems continue, you can contact the BBMP office or raise a support request on the portal.

**BBMP E Khata** is the digital form of a property&#39;s Khata record maintained through the applicable BBMP digital property record system.

It contains important information related to the property, owner, taxation, and property identification. Digital property records can make it easier for owners to access and manage their information.

- Property tax receipts
- Existing Khata documents
- Owner&#39;s identity proof
- Address proof
- Property identification details
- Building plan or approval documents, where applicable
- Conversion or sanction documents, where applicable
Property owners should verify the current requirements before submitting an application.

## A Khata vs B Khata BBMP

Understanding the difference between **A Khata and B Khata** is important before starting any property-related application.

### What is A Khata BBMP?

An **A Khata** generally relates to a property that meets the applicable municipal requirements and has the necessary approvals and documentation.

Depending on the property and applicable regulations, A Khata properties may have advantages such as:

- Better documentation status
- Easier property transactions
- Better access to certain financial services
- Eligibility for applicable building permissions
- Better resale prospects
However, Khata alone should not be considered a complete guarantee of legal title. Property owners should verify the complete property documentation.

### What is B Khata BBMP?

A **B Khata** generally refers to properties recorded separately for taxation purposes where there may be deviations, incomplete approvals, or other compliance-related issues.

Depending on the specific issue, B Khata properties may face:

- Difficulties with certain building approvals
- Challenges with some financial institutions
- Additional documentation requirements
- Complications during property transactions
- Need for further regularization or compliance
Each B Khata property should be assessed individually to determine the appropriate course of action.

## B Khata to A Khata Conversion

Property owners with B Khata records may want to explore whether their property is eligible for **B Khata to A Khata conversion**.

Conversion is not automatic and depends on the property&#39;s documents, land status, approvals, building compliance, and applicable rules.

### General Process for B Khata to A Khata Conversion

The process may generally involve:

#### 1. Property Document Verification

Review the sale deed, title documents, tax records, Khata records, EC, and other relevant documents.

#### 2. Check Compliance

Identify any missing approvals, building deviations, land-related issues, or other compliance requirements.

#### 3. Clear Property Tax Dues

Check for outstanding property tax and other applicable dues and clear them where required.

#### 4. Prepare the Application

Prepare the applicable application and supporting documents according to the current procedure.

#### 5. Pay Applicable Charges

Where applicable, conversion, betterment, regularization, or other charges may need to be paid.

#### 6. Verification

The submitted documents and property details may be reviewed by the concerned authority.

#### 7. Updated Khata Record

If the property meets the applicable requirements and the application is approved, the Khata record may be updated accordingly.

Because eligibility can vary from property to property, professional document verification can help identify potential issues before applying.

## Khata Bifurcation BBMP

**Khata bifurcation** is the process of separating an existing property record into separate records when a property is divided or ownership is separated.

Khata bifurcation may be required when:

- Property is inherited by multiple legal heirs
- Joint owners divide their property
- A larger property is legally divided
- A site is subdivided
- Ownership is separated after partition
- Separate property records are required for eligible units

### Documents for Khata Bifurcation

Depending on the circumstances, documents may include:

- Sale deed
- Partition deed
- Gift deed, where applicable
- Will or inheritance documents, where applicable
- Property tax receipts
- Existing Khata documents
- Identity proof
- Relevant property plans
- Other supporting documents
The exact requirements depend on the reason for bifurcation and the property&#39;s documentation.

## BBMP Khata Transfer

**BBMP Khata transfer** may be required when ownership of a property changes due to a sale, inheritance, gift, or other legally recognized transfer.

Before applying for Khata transfer, property owners should ensure that:

- The ownership document is properly registered
- Property tax records are updated
- Property details are accurate
- Supporting documents are available
- Any applicable dues are cleared
The required procedure may vary depending on the nature of the ownership transfer.

## Common Problems During BBMP E Khata Application

Property owners may face several issues during the application process.

### Incorrect Owner Details

The owner&#39;s name may be different across the sale deed, tax record, Khata record, or digital property record.

### Property Number Mismatch

Differences in property numbers or identification details can cause verification issues.

### Tax Record Discrepancies

Pending taxes or differences in tax records may need to be resolved.

### Missing Documents

Applications may be delayed when required supporting documents are unavailable or incomplete.

### Building Approval Issues

Properties with deviations or missing approvals may face additional complications.

### Digital Record Errors

Incorrect information in the existing digital record may require a correction request before completing another property-related process.

## How to Avoid BBMP E Khata Application Delays

Property owners can reduce avoidable delays by:

- Checking all property documents before applying
- Ensuring the owner&#39;s name is consistent
- Verifying property measurements
- Checking property tax status
- Keeping the latest EC available
- Scanning documents clearly
- Checking the application details before submission
- Retaining acknowledgement and application details
- Resolving known discrepancies before applying
